solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Coach second half of train lost

indicators.note: half of the word means only its first part is kept

parts.note: choo-choo is a child's word for a railway train
L is an abbreviation for lost, as in football results tables

explanation.surface: A railway passenger finds that half of the train has gone missing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Coach' looks like a railway carriage to go with the train, but it is the verb meaning to teach.
explanation.definitionFit: To coach someone is to train or teach them, and to school a pupil is the same thing.

clue.text: Revolutionary column about extremely ebullient slave

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the shuffled letters go around the others
something revolutionary turns things over, so the letters of column are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, as anagram fodder

indicators.note: the extremes of a word are its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A newspaper column by a radical writer seems unusually cheerful about something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Revolutionary' reworks the letters of column, giving UNCLOM; 'extremely' takes the outer letters of ebullient, which 'about' puts in.
explanation.definitionFit: The title character of Harriet Beecher Stowe's novel is an enslaved man, so the name stands for a slave.

clue.text: Type of company Scot takes home before opening time? Drunken sot!

indicators.note: takes means the Scot's name holds the other pieces inside it

parts.note: Jock is a familiar nickname for a Scotsman
in means at home

indicators.note: the opening of a word is its first letter
drunken suggests the letters stagger about into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, as anagram fodder

explanation.surface: A drunken Scotsman heads home just before the pub opens.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drunken' rearranges sot; 'opening' takes the first letter of time; 'takes' puts all of these within the Scot's nickname.
explanation.definitionFit: A joint-stock company is one whose capital is held jointly by shareholders, a standard business form.

clue.text: Drug not 15 for L

indicators.note: not means the letters of the cross-referenced answer are left out

parts.note: the drug is the opiate made from morphine, heroin
15 is ALL THE RAGE, which means fashionable, that is in

explanation.surface: A cryptic instruction that reads as bare mechanism: a drug, minus another answer, standing for a letter.
explanation.walkthrough: Throughout this puzzle L stands for lover. 15 down is ALL THE RAGE, a synonym of IN.
explanation.definitionFit: Hero was the priestess of Aphrodite whose lover Leander swam the Hellespont nightly to reach her.

clue.text: L showing passion, over Henry and Richard?

parts.note: heat means intensity of feeling, passion
H is the abbreviation for henry, the unit of inductance
the singer Cliff Richard; the question mark signals his first name is wanted

explanation.surface: A lover shows passion over two men called Henry and Richard.
explanation.walkthrough: L means lover throughout. 'over' sets HEAT above the rest in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: The brooding hero of Wuthering Heights is Catherine Earnshaw's passionate lover.

clue.text: Plant gangster next to L regularly

parts.note: Al Capone is the archetypal gangster

indicators.note: regularly means every other letter of the word for the lover is dropped, keeping the even ones

parts.note: in this puzzle L stands for lover

explanation.surface: A gangster plants something beside a lover at regular intervals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' takes the second and fourth letters of LOVER, giving OE.
explanation.definitionFit: Aloe is a succulent plant whose sap is used in soothing creams.

clue.text: One sets gems

parts.note: an means one, as in an apple
gels means sets, as a jelly does

explanation.surface: A jeweller who sets precious stones.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sets gems' reads as a jeweller at work, but 'sets' is a verb meaning firms up.
explanation.definitionFit: Calling people gems or treasures is affectionate praise, and so is calling them angels.

clue.text: Fellow, say, getting off with date? It's time to celebrate

indicators.note: getting off suggests things set loose and jumbled, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, as anagram fodder
taken as written, as anagram fodder

explanation.surface: A man who gets off with his date has good reason to celebrate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting off' looks like romance but signals the rearrangement of say and date, giving EASTDAY.
explanation.definitionFit: A feast day is a religious festival in the church calendar, a day set aside for celebration.

clue.text: Style of cooking Chekhov perhaps used for a gas in Cheddar?

indicators.note: used for means one piece takes the place of another

parts.note: Cheddar is a kind of cheese
He is the chemical symbol for helium, a gas
Anton Chekhov, the Russian playwright; perhaps signals that Anton is an example of a first name

explanation.surface: A recipe puzzle: could a Russian writer replace a gas inside a cheese?
explanation.walkthrough: In CHEESE the HE is swapped for ANTON, which 'used for' signals.
explanation.definitionFit: The cuisine of Guangdong province in southern China is the most widely known Chinese cooking style abroad.

clue.text: Chap wanting good peep shows

indicators.note: wanting means lacking, so the letter is removed

parts.note: a glance is a quick peep

explanation.surface: A man who has no good peep shows to watch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chap wanting' reads as a man who wants something, but 'wanting' takes G out of GLANCE.
explanation.definitionFit: Lance is a man's first name, and a chap in crosswords is any man's name.

clue.text: L drunk as a lord? No!

indicators.note: drunk suggests the letters reel into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, as anagram fodder
taken as written, as anagram fodder

explanation.surface: Is the lover as drunk as a lord? No!
explanation.walkthrough: L means lover throughout; 'drunk' rearranges A LORD and NO.
explanation.definitionFit: In As You Like It, the young man who pins love poems to trees in Arden is Rosalind's lover.

clue.text: Greek 4 from area around 11?

parts.note: 4 down is a hero; 11 across is a city in Florida, so its area reads as the south-east of the United States

explanation.surface: A Greek hero hailing from the region around Orlando.
explanation.walkthrough: 11 across is ORLANDO, and Orlando, Florida lies in the south-east US, so the clue reads as THE SE US. 4 down is HERO.
explanation.definitionFit: The Athenian who slew the Minotaur is one of the great heroes of Greek myth.

clue.text: Those flying westward from right to left

indicators.note: reading westward, from right to left, means taking the letters backwards

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for left; that the letters also run backwards inside the clue's to left is a coincidence of this parse

explanation.surface: Birds flying west, heading from right to left across the map.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to left' gives TOL, which 'westward from right' reads backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: LOT is the Polish national airline, so its planes and crews are literally those flying.

clue.text: Dogged by ill luck, as Ls may be

definitions.meaning: plagued by misfortune, born under unlucky stars
L is lover in this puzzle, and Shakespeare calls Romeo and Juliet a pair of ill-fated lovers in this phrase

explanation.surface: Lovers dogged by misfortune.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means thwarted by malign fate, from the prologue to Romeo and Juliet.

clue.text: Very cool heart? Legal troubles!

indicators.note: troubles means disturbs, so the letters are stirred up

parts.note: taken as written, as anagram fodder
taken as written, as anagram fodder

explanation.surface: A heart-to-heart about legal troubles: hardly cool.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heart' looks like part of the definition, but 'troubles' rearranges HEART and LEGAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that is all the rage is highly fashionable, which is what very cool means.

clue.text: Gave rise to new journalist following rising firm (an electronics company)

indicators.note: in a down clue, rising means the word is read upwards, backwards

parts.note: CO is the abbreviation for company, a firm
Casio is the Japanese maker of calculators and watches
ED is the abbreviation for editor, a journalist

explanation.surface: A new reporter joins a rising electronics firm, which causes something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rising' reads the firm upwards in this down entry; 'following' places new and journalist after it.
explanation.definitionFit: To occasion an event is to cause it, a formal synonym of bringing about.

clue.text: L spelt with a capital O

parts.note: Rome is the capital of Italy

explanation.surface: A letter L written with a capital O, like a lettering instruction.
explanation.walkthrough: L means lover throughout; 'spelt with' just joins the capital city to O.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare's young Montague is the archetypal lover.

clue.text: L featuring in a Lord's game

indicators.note: game means ready to play along, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, as anagram fodder
taken as written, as anagram fodder

explanation.surface: A lover playing in a game at Lord's, the London cricket ground.
explanation.walkthrough: Lord's is the famous London cricket ground, which 'game' plays on. 'game' rearranges IN and A LORDS.
explanation.definitionFit: In As You Like It the heroine disguised as Ganymede is Orlando's beloved and lover.

clue.text: In Bucharest, readies some incredible instruments

indicators.note: some means only a part of the words is taken, letters running across them

explanation.surface: Musicians in Bucharest get some amazing instruments ready.
explanation.walkthrough: 'readies' looks like a verb, but it is British slang for ready cash; 'some' takes the letters across incredible instruments.
explanation.definitionFit: The currency of Romania is the leu, plural lei, so in Bucharest that is the cash.

clue.text: Yacht rigged for L

indicators.note: rigged means fixed or set up crookedly, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A yacht fitted out with rigging for a lover.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rigged' looks nautical beside 'Yacht', but it rearranges the letters. L means lover.
explanation.definitionFit: Catherine Earnshaw of Wuthering Heights, called by a pet name, is Heathcliff's lover.

clue.text: Broken hearts, including hearts with primarily strong beats

indicators.note: including means holding something inside
broken means smashed apart, so the letters are reassembled

parts.note: taken as written, as anagram fodder
H is the abbreviation for hearts in card games

indicators.note: primarily means first, so the first letter is taken

explanation.surface: Broken hearts beating strongly, a heartbreak scene.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Broken' turns HEARTS into THRASE, 'including' puts H inside after the A, and 'primarily' adds S from strong.
explanation.definitionFit: To thrash is to beat soundly, so a team that thrashes rivals beats them.

clue.text: Endure periods working gear levers in the US

parts.note: to stick something out is to endure it
shifts are periods of work

explanation.surface: A mechanic puts in long shifts fixing gear levers.
explanation.definitionFit: Americans call a manual gearbox and its lever a stick shift.

clue.text: Prepared to fight, as brother might be

definitions.meaning: a comrade-soldier is a brother so described

explanation.surface: A brother who is ready for a fight.
explanation.definitionFit: To be up in arms is to be armed and ready to fight; a fellow soldier is a brother in arms.

clue.text: Initially 17 across and 24 rule in India

indicators.note: initially means taking the first letters of each word

explanation.surface: Two lovers named together, with a note on Indian rule.
explanation.walkthrough: 17 across is ROMEO and 24 down is JULIET; 'Initially' takes R, A and J.
explanation.definitionFit: The Raj was British rule over India, from the Hindi word for reign.

clue.text: L with project involving romance

indicators.note: involving means wrapping around another piece

parts.note: to jut is to project or stick out
to romance is to tell fanciful untruths, that is to lie

explanation.surface: A lover with a romantic project.
explanation.walkthrough: 'romance' looks like love, but it is the verb to fib; 'project' is a verb too. L means lover.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare's Capulet daughter is the most famous lover in drama.

clue.text: Boss around new L

indicators.note: around means one piece wraps the other

parts.note: a leader is a boss

explanation.surface: A boss bossing a new lover around.
explanation.walkthrough: N goes inside LEADER, which 'around' signals. L means lover.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth the young man who swam the Hellespont to reach Hero was her lover.

clue.text: Movement lawyer repeated

indicators.note: repeated means the piece is written twice

parts.note: DA is a district attorney, an American prosecuting lawyer

explanation.surface: A lawyer's motion, filed twice over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Movement' looks like a legal motion, but it is an art movement.
explanation.definitionFit: Dada was the anti-art movement founded in Zurich during the First World War.

clue.text: Like committed Ls, Paul's so bubbly

indicators.note: bubbly means effervescent, so the letters fizz into a new order

explanation.surface: Paul is so cheerful about a pair of committed lovers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bubbly' looks like champagne at a wedding, but it rearranges PAULS SO.
explanation.definitionFit: Committed lovers who marry become husband and wife, so their relation is marital.

clue.text: Fit one of 4 in costume

definitions.meaning: to fit is to be right for, as in that colour becomes you
a pack of cards has four groups: hearts, clubs, diamonds and spades
an outfit of matching jacket and trousers

explanation.surface: Fitting someone into one of four costumes.
explanation.definitionFit: The word covers being right for, a card group of which there are four, and a matching outfit.

clue.text: Fellow coming round in the morning? That's flipping Wanderer!

indicators.note: flipping means turning over, so the whole is read backwards
coming round means wrapping around another piece

parts.note: a don is a fellow of a university college
AM is the abbreviation for the morning

explanation.surface: The setter Wanderer drops in on a fellow one morning, flippantly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coming round' sets the morning inside the fellow, giving DAMON, and 'flipping' reverses it. Wanderer is also the setter's own name.
explanation.definitionFit: A nomad is a member of a people who roam with no fixed home, a wanderer.

clue.text: L from African republic, almost always seen cycling around

indicators.note: almost means the last letter is dropped

parts.note: Guinea is a republic in West Africa

indicators.note: cycling around means the first letter is moved to the end

parts.note: ever means always

explanation.surface: A lover from Africa who is always seen out on a bicycle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' trims the country's last letter; 'cycling around' moves the first letter of the word for always to its end, making VERE.
explanation.definitionFit: Arthur's queen in the Camelot legends was the lover of Sir Lancelot.
